title: World Liberty Financial + USD1 - the Trump-family stablecoin and its conflict-of-interest web
source: Public record: WLFI/USD1 disclosures; Forbes/Fortune/WSJ/Reuters/CoinDesk/The Block reporting; Senate (Warren et al.) inquiry letters. Deepens the existing WLFI node into USD1 + the MGX/Binance/UAE nexus. HONESTY DOCTRINE APPLIES: deals, dates, ownership %, and the MGX settlement are documented fact (figures are reported estimates that shift over time); the emoluments-clause characterization is legal-experts' OPINION (contested), not an adjudicated finding; the 'FTX-circular' comparison is reported + interpretation. No partisan claim is made - the map records documented ties + labeled concerns.
grade: per-edge in notes (fact | reported/varies | contested/legal-opinion | interpretation)

edges.notes: WLFI (DeFi venture co-founded by Trump + his three sons, debuted Oct 2024; ~$550M WLFI token sale) issues USD1 - a USD-deposit + T-bill-backed stablecoin launched Mar 2025. USD1 grew from ~$3B (Dec 2025) to ~$4.6B (Apr 2026), reported the fastest-growing stablecoin ever - but growth was largely NON-organic (deal-driven, Binance-concentrated) (fact of issuance/dates; supply figures reported/varies; 'non-organic' interpretation).
USD1 is a fiat-backed stablecoin (USD deposits + Treasuries) - politically distinctive but mechanically similar to USDC/USDT; it sits in the same reserve-income model (fact).
USD1 reserves are held in USD deposits + T-bills - adding the Trump-linked issuer to the stablecoin-Treasury rail (float -> Treasuries -> issuer reserve income) (fact of backing model).

USD1 supply is heavily concentrated at Binance (~$4.7B of USD1 in Binance accounts as of early 2026; split between exchange + customers unclear); Binance added USD1 trading pairs, elevating the token (fact of concentration; ownership split unclear/reported).

Abu Dhabi state-backed fund MGX chose USD1 to settle its ~$2B minority investment in Binance (announced Token2049 Dubai, 1 May 2025, by Zach Witkoff with Eric Trump + Justin Sun) - reportedly the largest crypto-settled investment ever; MGX cited 'compliance history' though USD1 was then brand-new (fact of deal; the 'compliance history' rationale noted as ironic/graded).
Zach Witkoff co-founded WLFI + fronted the MGX/USD1-Binance announcement; son of Trump envoy Steve Witkoff - the political-family + Gulf-diplomacy overlap that defines the venture (fact).

Per WSJ (reported Jan 2026), a deal was signed ~Jan 2025 for lieutenants of Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed to acquire ~49% of WLFI for ~$500M; Tahnoon also chairs MGX (which then settled $2B in USD1 into Binance) + G42 - the UAE<->WLFI<->MGX<->Binance loop; subsequent US approval of advanced-chip exports to the UAE drew emoluments-clause concerns from legal experts (fact of reported deal + concerns; the ~49%/$500M = reported; emoluments = contested legal opinion).

Conflict-of-interest nexus: a Trump-family LLC reportedly owns ~38% of WLFI + is entitled to 75% of WLFI token proceeds while Trump holds office (reported ~$1B realized + ~$3B unsold by Dec 2025, estimates vary); Senate Democrats (Warren et al.) sought probes over token buyers + the UAE deal. The map records the documented arrangement + the raised concerns; it makes no adjudicated legal claim (fact of arrangement/inquiries; profit figures reported/varies; wrongdoing contested).

WLFI is central to the crypto-ethics fight that helped stall CLARITY: ethics language targeting the President's ~$1.4B crypto income (WLFI/USD1) was one of the three unresolved disputes at the failed 15 Sep 2026 cloture vote (fact of the sticking point; see spec-clarity-act-chronology).
